# Adjudication Task — Chapter 887

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃887화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|스아아아.
  6|
  7|용암과도 같은 열기가 수많은 혈도를 뜨겁게 달구며 휘몰아친다.
  8|
  9|나는 타오르는 눈동자로 소교를 노려보았다. 숨결과 함께 흘러나오는 목소리는 잿가루처럼 퍼석했다.
 10|
 11|“당신…… 도대체 뭐야?”
 12|
 13|“반응이 격하네. 적당히 하고 공력을 가라앉히는 게 좋을 거야.”
 14|
 15|소교가, 아니…… 이제는 누구인지 모를 그녀가 대답했다.
 16|
 17|언제나 그렇듯 담담하고 차분하게.
 18|
 19|하지만 지금껏 스스로를 포장하던 존댓말과 예의 바른 태도를 벗어던진 채.
 20|
 21|그리고 다음 순간 그녀의 입술 사이로 흘러나온 한마디가, 마치 격랑처럼 일어나 나를 덮쳤다.
 22|
 23|“지금 몸 상태를 생각한다면 더더욱. 안 그래?”
 24|
 25|“……!”
 26|
 27|벼락에 정수리를 관통당한다면 아마 이런 기분일까.
 28|
 29|나도 모르게 파르르 떨리는 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
 30|
 31|“어……떻게?”
 32|
 33|“공력의 흐름이 불안정하니까.”
 34|
 35|소교의 대답은 짧고 간단했으며, 무엇보다 반박할 여지가 없는 정론(正論)이었다.
 36|
 37|그러나 내가 순간 할 말을 잃어버린 이유는 따로 있었다.
 38|
 39|저 당연한 대답을 위해서는 한 가지의 전제 조건이 필요하니까.
 40|
 41|‘기감(氣感).’
 42|
 43|그것도 극도로 뛰어난, 칼날처럼 예리한 감각.
 44|
 45|모든 전투는 상대를 가늠하는 것으로 시작된다.
 46|
 47|고수는 하수가 지닌 공력의 크기와 그 상태를 꿰뚫어 보지만, 하수는 고수의 정확한 수준을 제대로 가늠하지 못한다.
 48|
 49|그리고 지금의 나는…… 명백한 후자(後者)다.
 50|
 51|‘고수!’
 52|
 53|틀림없다.
 54|
 55|눈앞의 저 여인, 소교는 실로 엄청난 고수였다.
 56|
 57|심지어 내 눈을 속일 정도로 완벽하게 스스로를 숨길 수 있는, 반박귀진(返璞歸眞)의 경지에 도달한 초절정 고수.
 58|
 59|‘앞서 보였던 그 움직임이, 우연이 아니었어.’
 60|
 61|터져 나오려는 탄식을 애써 억누른 나는 조용히 주먹을 말아 쥐었다.
 62|
 63|그럴듯한 무기 하나 없는 적수공권(赤手空拳)에 불안정한 몸 상태까지.
 64|
 65|제아무리 긍정적으로 생각해 보아도 한 수 위의 고수를 상대하기에는 좋지 않은 상황이었지만, 나는 자세를 비스듬히 낮춘 채 재차 공력을 끌어 올렸다.
 66|
 67|“누구냐, 너.”
 68|
 69|소교가 담담한 목소리로 대답했다.
 70|
 71|“그 물음에 답해 줄 의무는 없지. 먼저 약속을 어기고 거짓말한 건 너였으니까, 열화신룡 진태경.”
 72|
 73|“아가리 닥치고 대답이나 해. 정확히 누구의 명령을 따르고 있지? 황제? 아니면…….”
 74|
 75|나는 소교를 노려보며 두 글자를 씹어뱉었다.
 76|
 77|“천주(天主)?”
 78|
 79|“글쎄.”
 80|
 81|잠깐의 침묵.
 82|
 83|도무지 그 의중을 짐작할 수 없는, 모호한 표정으로 나를 물끄러미 바라보던 소교가 불쑥 입을 열었다.
 84|
 85|“내가 누구인지 알면, 그런다고 해서 뭐가 달라질까?”
 86|
 87|“달라지겠지. 생사(生死)가 걸린 문제니까.”
 88|
 89|“생사라…….”
 90|
 91|“그래. 대답 여하에 따라 이 자리의 누군가는 반드시 죽는다.”
 92|
 93|“만약 그렇게 된다면 죽을 사람은 이미 정해져 있네. 안 그래?”
 94|
 95|그 순간.
 96|
 97|스아아아.
 98|
 99|공기가 파르르 떨렸다.
100|
101|바람이 되어 풀과 꽃을 뒤흔드는 그 기세는 북풍(北風)과도 같았고, 서늘한 눈빛과 목소리는 설한(雪寒)이 되어 나를 휘감는다.
102|
103|하지만 나는 동요하지 않았다.
104|
105|단지 상대가 강적이라는 이유 하나만으로 두려움을 느끼기에는 이미 내가 헤쳐 온 수라장이 너무 많았다.
106|
107|헌터로서도, 무림인으로서도.
108|
109|“그래, 어느 정도는 정해져 있을지도 모르지. 하지만 꼭 둘 중 하나만 죽어야 한다는 법이라도 있나.”
110|
111|“뭐?”
112|
113|“넌 내가 죽인다. 반드시.”
114|
115|“……!”
116|
117|“내 모든 걸 걸고 약속. 아니, 장담하지.”
118|
119|나 스스로도 내심 놀랄 만큼 무덤덤한 목소리.
120|
121|그러나 이건 결코 위기에 몰린 약자가 보이는 허장성세(虛張聲勢) 따위가 아니었고, 내 확신은 고스란히 소교에게 전해졌다.
122|
123|“너…… 진심이구나?”
124|
125|“당연히.”
126|
127|“동귀어진(同歸於盡)이라. 하.”
128|
129|작게 헛웃음을 흘린 소교가 신기한 동물 보듯이 나를 위아래로 훑었다.
130|
131|“역시 그 정보들이 사실이었네. 하긴, 뭔가 숨겨 둔 한 수라도 있으니 지금까지 살아남을 수 있었겠지.”
132|
133|“혈주와 서천마군, 가장 최근에는 남천마후까지. 물론 위기마다 검성(劍星)이나 화왕(火王)의 도움이 있었다고는 해도, 그들을 상대하고도 무사하다는 건 불가능에 가까운 일이니까.”
134|
135|“……!”
136|
137|나는 깊게 가라앉은 눈으로 소교를 응시했다.
138|
139|조금 전 물음의 대답은 굳이 듣지 않아도 될 것 같다는 생각과 함께.
140|
141|‘이 여자, 서천마군과 남천마후에 대해 알고 있다.’
142|
143|그것도 단지 정보로만 접한 것이 아니라 그들이 어떤 인물이었는지, 어느 수준의 강자였는지 알고 있다는 투다.
144|
145|마치 예전부터 일면식이 있던 것처럼.
146|
147|비로소 소교라는 이름과 신분으로 정체를 감춘 저 여자의 배후가 선명하게 그려졌다.
148|
149|‘……암천(暗天).’
150|
151|그래, 그것밖에는 없다.
152|
153|심지어 저 입으로 직접 밝히기까지 하지 않았나.
154|
155|자신이 황궁에 머무르는 가장 큰 이유 중 하나는, 그 방대한 정보력 때문이라고.
156|
157|이는 소교가 황제의 충복이 아니라는 뜻인 동시에 또 다른 목적을 갖고 있음을 의미했다.
158|
159|‘황궁을, 아니…… 황제를 손아귀에 쥐고 흔들 셈이었겠지.’
160|
161|조각조각 흩어져 있던 퍼즐이 맞아떨어진다.
162|
163|사 황자의 갑작스러운 반란. 선황을 비롯한 직계 황족들의 죽음과 지금에 이르기까지.
164|
165|그러나 결과적으로는 절반의 성공에 지나지 않았다.
166|
167|하루아침에 황제가 뒤바뀌고, 수많은 사람이 형장의 이슬로 사라졌어도 반대파를 완전히 뿌리 뽑아 대국 전체를 손에 넣는 것에는 실패했으니.
168|
169|‘그렇다면 혹시.’
170|
171|머릿속의 퍼즐이 거의 완성되려던 그때, 말없이 나를 바라보던 소교가 불쑥 입을 열었다.
172|
173|“하나만 묻자. 도대체 이렇게까지 하는 이유가 뭐야?”
174|
175|“이유?”
176|
177|“그래. 동귀어진마저 각오하는, 그 성치 않은 몸으로 굳이 내게 맞서려는 이유.”
178|
179|나는 잠시 침묵했다.
180|
181|그 이유에 대해 고민할 시간이 필요해서가 아니라, 나로서는 너무나도 당연한 일이었기 때문에.
182|
183|“그렇게라도 해야, 내 사람들이 덜 죽으니까.”
184|
185|“뭐?”
186|
187|“설령 이 자리에서 둘 다 죽는다고 해도, 너 같은 년을 살려 두는 것보다는 훨씬 나을 테니까.”
188|
189|“내가 지금 널 해할 생각이 없다고 해도?”
190|
191|“당연히 헛소리겠지만, 물론.”
192|
193|“어째서?”
194|
195|“너처럼 독사 같은 년은 오래 살수록 해악이 되거든.”
196|
197|그동안 얼마나 많은 이들이 죽었나.
198|
199|암천이 한 번 움직일 때마다 수백이, 수천이, 끝내는 수만이나 되는 사람들이 고혼이 되어 사라졌다.
200|
201|그러니 나 한 사람으로 퉁칠 수 있다면 오히려 다행이다.
202|
203|물론 내가 살아남고 소교가 죽는다면 그것이야말로 최고의 결과겠지만…….
204|
205|“아무래도 상관없어. 그 빌어먹을 독니 뽑고, 가죽까지 싹 벗겨 놔야 마음이 홀가분할 것 같으니까.”
206|
207|이번에 침묵을 택한 것은 소교였다.
208|
209|한참이나 입을 굳게 다물고 있던 그녀는 한마디를 툭, 내던졌다.
210|
211|“이거, 생각했던 것보다 훨씬 미친놈이네?”
212|
213|“뭐라는 거야, 미친년이.”
214|
215|“그리고 상산왕, 그 어린아이가 왜 그리 널 따르는지 조금은 알 것 같네. 응, 확실히.”
216|
217|“지금…… 어린애 하나 인질로 잡았다고 협박하는 거냐?”
218|
219|“글쎄, 어떨까.”
220|
221|“어떻긴, 씨발. 무슨 짓을 해서든 널 죽여야 하는 이유가 하나 더 생긴 거지.”
222|
223|“의욕 넘치고 좋네. 하지만 모든 일이 마음먹은 대로 흘러가는 건 아니지.”
224|
225|소교가 작게 고개를 내저었다.
226|
227|“그 나이에 벌써 이 정도의 경지에 다다르다니, 하늘의 장난이라고 생각될 만큼 대단한 재능이고 성취야. 그것만큼은 누구도 부정할 수 없어. 하지만…….”
228|
229|그녀가 천천히 말을 이었다.
230|
231|“모든 것에는 때가 있는 법이란다. 천기(天氣)를 타고 났다고 해서 죽음마저 피할 수 있는 건 아니거든.”
232|
233|스륵.
234|
235|옷깃을 스치는 미세한 소음.
236|
237|동시에 소교의 가느다란 허리춤을 감싸고 있던 요대. 아니, 한 자루의 연검(軟劍)이 막강한 공력을 머금은 채 나를 향해 겨누어졌다.
238|
239|그 낭창한 검신 너머로 보이는 서늘한 눈동자와 함께.
240|
241|“하늘이 널 구해 줄지, 아니면 이대로 죽게 내버려 둘지…… 이참에 한번 시험해 볼까?”
242|
243|우우우웅.
244|
245|그리고 낮지만 또렷한 검명(劍鳴)이 울려 퍼진 그 순간.
246|
247|화아악.
248|
249|나는 똑똑히 느낄 수 있었다.
250|
251|지금껏 느끼지 못했던, 실로 끔찍하리만치 거대한 기운이 소교를 중심으로 퍼져 나가는 것을.
252|
253|내 전신을 빈틈없이 옥죄고 짓누르는 것을.
254|
255|흐읍.
256|
257|나도 모르게 들이켠 호흡.
258|
259|삽시간에 무거워진 공기가 숨통을 조인다.
260|
261|피부로 느껴지는 그 막강한 기세에 온몸의 솜털이 곤두서고 식은땀이 맺혔다.
262|
263|하지만.
264|
265|“좆, 까.”
266|
267|씹어뱉듯 토해 낸 한마디와 함께, 나는 보리지 않는 공력의 사슬을 밀어냈다.
268|
269|내 팔과 다리를 꽁꽁 묶어 오는 그것을 버텨 내며 소교를 향해 나아갔다.
270|
271|콰드득. 푹.
272|
273|한 걸음.
274|
275|고작 한 걸음일 뿐일진대, 발밑의 단단한 청석(靑石)이 단숨에 박살 나고 그 아래에 층층이 쌓여 있던 지면이 움푹 꺼진다.
276|
277|단순히 내 몸무게가 그만큼 무거워서? 아니면 오랫동안 방치되었던 이 장소가 그만큼 낡아 있어서?
278|
279|둘 다 틀렸다.
280|
281|천 근, 만 근에 달하는 공력의 압력을 고스란히 받아 내며 내디딘 걸음이기 때문이다.
282|
283|또한 공력으로 공력을 해소한 것이 아닌, 이미 인간의 한계를 아득히 벗어난 신체 능력만으로 이를 버텼기 때문이다.
284|
285|우득. 콰드드득.
286|
287|다시 한번 힘을 실어 내디딘 발끝이 흙과 꽃을 지르밟는다. 이미 앞서 산산이 부서졌던 청석 조각들이 수십, 수백으로 으스러지는 것이 느껴졌다.
288|
289|한 걸음, 한 걸음 가까워질수록 더욱더 강해지는 압력도 함께.
290|
291|하지만…….
292|
293|‘버틸 수 있다.’
294|
295|잘 벼려 낸 날붙이는 그 자체로도 훌륭한 무기인 법. 지금껏 숱하게 사선(死線)을 넘나들며 성장해 온 신체 능력 역시 마찬가지였다.
296|
297|근력. 체력. 민첩.
298|
299|그 모든 면에서 나는 월등했다. 한계를 뛰어넘었다.
300|

*So that movement earlier wasn’t a fluke.*

[P25]
I held back a gasp and quietly clenched my fists.

[P26]

[P27]
Still, I lowered my stance at an angle and drew up my internal energy again.

[P28]
“Who are you?”

[P29]
So Gyo answered calmly.

[P30]
“I have no obligation to tell you. You were the one who broke your promise and lied first, Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.”

[P31]

[P32]

[P33]
“Lord of Heaven?”

[P34]
“Who knows.”

[P35]

[P36]
“If you knew who I was, what would that change?”

[P37]
“It would change things. Lives are at stake.”

[P38]
“Lives…”

[P39]
“Yeah. Depending on your answer, someone here is going to die.”

[P40]
“If it comes to that, we already know who it’ll be. Don’t we?”

[P41]
At that moment—

[P42]
Sssshhh.

[P43]
The air trembled. Her aura stirred the grass and flowers like a north wind, while her cold gaze and voice wrapped around me like winter frost.

[P44]
But I didn’t waver.

[P45]
I’d been through too many bloodbaths to fear someone just because she was strong—as a Hunter and as a martial artist of Murim.

[P46]
“Yeah, maybe we do know. But who says only one of us has to die?”

[P47]
“What?”

[P48]
“I’ll kill you. No matter what.”

[P49]
“……!”

[P50]
“I swear on everything I have. No—I guarantee it.”

[P51]
My voice was so calm it surprised even me.

[P52]

[P53]
“You… you’re serious?”

[P54]
“Of course.”

[P55]
“So you’re willing to die taking me with you. Ha.”

[P56]
She gave a short, disbelieving laugh and looked me up and down like some strange animal.

[P57]
“So the reports were true after all. I suppose you must have something up your sleeve to have survived this long.”

[P58]
“The Blood Lord, the Western Heaven Demon Lord, and most recently, even the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. The Sword Saint and the Fire King helped you through those crises, of course, but coming through encounters with all of them unharmed is nearly impossible.”

[P59]
“……!”

[P60]
I stared at her, my gaze turning cold.

[P61]
I had a feeling I no longer needed to hear the answer to my question.

[P62]
*She knows about the Western Heaven Demon Lord and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.*

[P63]
She didn’t sound as though she merely knew their names from reports. She spoke as if she knew what kind of people they were and how powerful they were—as if she’d met them before.

[P64]
At last, I could see who stood behind the name and identity of So Gyo.

[P65]
*…Dark Heaven.*

[P66]
Yeah. What else could it be?

[P67]
Hadn’t she said herself that one of the main reasons she stayed in the imperial palace was its vast intelligence network? She wasn’t a loyal servant of the Emperor. She had another purpose.

[P68]
*She meant to get the imperial palace—or rather, the Emperor—in her grip and pull the strings.*

[P69]
The scattered pieces fell into place: the Fourth Prince’s sudden rebellion, the deaths of the late Emperor and his direct descendants, and everything that had happened since.

[P70]
But in the end, it had only been a partial success.

[P71]
The Emperor had been replaced overnight, and countless people had gone to their deaths on the execution grounds. Even so, they’d failed to root out all opposition and take control of the entire Great Nation.

[P72]
*Then could it be…*

[P73]
Just as the last pieces were about to fall into place, So Gyo broke her silence.

[P74]
“Let me ask you one thing. Why go this far?”

[P75]
“Why?”

[P76]
“Why fight me when your body’s in such poor shape? You’re even prepared to die taking me down.”

[P77]

[P78]
“Because fewer of my people will die if I do.”

[P79]
“What?”

[P80]
“Even if we both die here, that’s better than letting a bitch like you live.”

[P81]
“What if I said I had no intention of harming you?”

[P82]
“That’s obviously bullshit, but sure.”

[P83]
“Why?”

[P84]
“Because a viper like you only does more harm the longer she lives.”

[P85]
How many people had died already?

[P86]
Every time Dark Heaven made a move, hundreds died. Then thousands. Eventually, tens of thousands vanished, leaving only lonely ghosts.

[P87]
If my life was enough to put an end to that, I’d count myself lucky. Of course, the best outcome would be for me to live and So Gyo to die…

[P88]
“But I don’t care either way. I won’t feel right until I’ve pulled out those damn fangs and stripped your skin off.”

[P89]
This time, So Gyo fell silent. She kept her lips pressed together for a long while before tossing out a single remark.

[P90]
“You’re even crazier than I thought.”

[P91]
“What the hell are you talking about, you crazy bitch?”

[P92]
“And I think I understand a little of why Prince Shangshan, that child, is so attached to you. Yes, I do.”

[P93]
“Are you threatening me because you’ve got a kid hostage?”

[P94]
“Who knows?”

[P95]
“What do you mean, ‘who knows’? Fuck. You’ve just given me one more reason to kill you, whatever it takes.”

[P96]
“I like the enthusiasm. But things don’t always go the way you want.”

[P97]
So Gyo shook her head slightly.

[P98]
“To have reached this realm at your age… Your talent and what you’ve achieved are so remarkable they seem like a trick of heaven. No one could deny that. But…”

[P99]
She went on slowly.

[P100]
“Everything has its time, child. Even being born blessed by heaven won’t let you escape death.”

[P101]
Swish.

[P102]
I heard a faint sound against her collar.

[P103]
The belt around So Gyo’s slender waist unfurled—no, it was a flexible sword. Filled with powerful internal energy, its blade pointed straight at me.

[P104]
Beyond it, her eyes were cold.

[P105]
“Shall we put it to the test? See whether heaven saves you or leaves you to die here?”

[P106]
Whoooom.

[P107]
A low, clear sword hum rang out.

[P108]
Fwoosh.

[P109]
Then I felt it unmistakably: an enormous, terrifying aura spreading from So Gyo, one I hadn’t sensed until now.

[P110]
It closed around my whole body, pressing down on every part of me.

[P111]
I drew in a breath without meaning to. The air had grown heavy in an instant, choking me. Every hair on my body stood on end, and cold sweat beaded on my skin.

[P112]
But—

[P113]
“Fuck off.”

[P114]
I spat the words through my teeth and pushed against the invisible chains of internal energy. They bound my arms and legs tight, but I withstood them and moved toward So Gyo.

[P115]
Crack. Thud.

[P116]
One step.

[P117]
Just one, and the solid bluestone beneath my foot shattered. The layers of earth below it caved in.

[P118]
Was I that heavy? Had this place grown so decrepit after being abandoned for so long?

[P119]
Neither.

[P120]
I’d taken that step under the full pressure of internal energy weighing a thousand geun—ten thousand geun. And I’d withstood it not by countering her internal energy with my own, but with physical strength that had long since surpassed human limits.

[P121]
Crunch. Craaack.

[P122]
I put more force into my next step, trampling soil and flowers underfoot. Beneath them, I felt the bluestone fragments break again into dozens, then hundreds of pieces.

[P123]
The closer I got, the stronger the pressure grew.

[P124]
But…

[P125]
*I can take it.*

[P126]
A well-honed blade was a fine weapon on its own. So was the body I’d built by surviving countless brushes with death.

[P127]
Strength. Stamina. Agility.

[P128]
I excelled in all three. I’d surpassed my limits.

[P129]
One of the main reasons I’d survived enemies a level—or even two levels—above me was this body, capable of superhuman feats without internal energy.

[P130]
It could tear steel apart with bare hands, run for two days and nights without collapsing, and surge forward like the wind with a single push off the ground.

[P131]
So even if several jiazi of internal energy closed around me, I could withstand it.

[P132]
No. I could break it.

[P133]
“Hah!”

[P134]
With a short shout, I threw both arms out with all my strength.

[P135]
Boom!

[P136]
The sheer force and speed burst through the compressed air. I felt the internal energy pressing down on me from every direction scatter.

[P137]
*Now!*

[P138]
My heavy body suddenly felt as light as a dandelion seed. I seized the opening and launched myself toward the one person staring at me with eyes now wide open.

[P139]
So Gyo.

[P140]
Fwoosh—boom!

[P141]
Flamefire Path.

[P142]
One step was all it took.

[P143]
Scorching Yang Qi surged up from deep within my dantian and exploded from my foot. I crossed the five jang between us in an instant, blazing heat trailing behind me, and drove my fist forward like a cannon shot.

[P144]
*BANG!*

[P145]
The world shook.

[P146]
Beyond the surging blue-white flames, a slender figure flew backward at tremendous speed to a roar that seemed to split the sky. Then she turned smoothly in midair.

[P147]
Tap.

[P148]
Her toes touched the blossom of a nameless flower, opened wide beneath the year’s strongest sunlight.

[P149]
So Gyo landed on that single flower as lightly as a passing breeze. I almost gasped.

[P150]
*Ah.*

[P151]
Elusive, yet graceful.

[P152]
Her movement technique was extraordinary. For an instant, I forgot she was my enemy. I even forgot I ought to press the attack while I had the chance.

[P153]
So Gyo’s eyes flashed with something I couldn’t read.

[P154]
“I couldn’t feel any internal energy from you at all… How did you do that?”

[P155]
I wanted to ask her the same thing.

[P156]
How had she blocked the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist I’d thrown with all my strength so easily? How had she met that blinding speed and force head-on without even looking strained?

[P157]
*You damn bitch. Have some decency and at least pretend that hurt.*

[P158]
I grumbled to myself and gave a rueful laugh.

[P159]
Why was I laughing now? I didn’t know. Maybe I really had gone crazy. Or maybe it was because I’d prepared myself to die before this fight began.

[P160]
Yeah. That was it.

[P161]
I’d been prepared for a long time.

[P162]
“You die, I live.”

[P163]
Laughing like a man half out of his mind, I took a step forward.

[P164]
My condition?

[P165]
Of course I wasn’t fine.

[P166]
After unleashing so much power at once, my dantian was already lurching like an overworked engine. My internal energy no longer moved as freely as my hands and feet.

[P167]
But this wasn’t a sport played in a ring. There was no referee to stop the match, no second to throw in the towel for a fighter in danger.

[P168]
That was what a life-and-death duel meant. I’d known it all along.

[P169]
*I’m ready.*

[P170]
My body might be failing, but my resolve didn’t waver.

[P171]
Holding fast to that single thought, I charged So Gyo again.

[P172]
Fwoosh!

[P173]
The world slowed. The scenery around me shifted.

[P174]
I gave myself over to the heat, the wind, and the fighting spirit bubbling through me like lava.

[P175]
Screeeech!

[P176]
With a piercing whistle, a streak of light hurtled toward me like lightning.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
